name: National Liberalism
summary: National liberalism fuses liberal demands for constitutional government, rule of law and a free economy with the project of building a strong nation-state. Its motto in Germany was that national unity and freedom must be won together by the same means, through gradual, constitutional reform rather than revolution. In practice it was a party of the educated and propertied middle class and big business, which backed a monarchical constitution, strong national power, the Kulturkampf against clerical influence, and, increasingly, military and colonial expansion.
scope: The German National Liberal Party of 1867 to 1918 (Bennigsen, Lasker, Miquel, Bassermann, early Stresemann), based on its June 1867 founding programme and historical accounts. It excludes other national-liberal traditions (Nordic, Romanian, Israeli, Korean and others) and the later nationalist drift of the party; answers on modern issues are mostly inferred.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nineteenth-century national liberals favoured self-help and a limited state; the party's attitude to Bismarck's social insurance was lukewarm, so a state-provided universal system is inferred as unwelcome.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Its programme attacks regulation of trades and labour and its later wing opposed welfare spending, so wage-setting by statute runs against its economic liberalism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The party championed a common market, currency and free trade in the 1870s and became the party of industry and banking, though it never opposed all state action.

public-ownership.rationale: A pro-business party of industry and banks would resist public ownership; Prussian railway nationalisation was a pragmatic exception, so this is inferred rather than stated.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Its base was the propertied and educated Protestant middle class and big business, which makes sharply higher taxes on the wealthy unlikely; no explicit tax doctrine was found.

unions-good.rationale: Its industrial wing was hostile to socialist organisation and it went along with the Anti-Socialist Laws, though some liberals backed non-socialist unions; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: It defended property and credit (the programme demands relief from the freezing of credit on real property) while accepting that law may regulate it, so strong but not absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The party became the voice of big industry and banks, so tighter regulation of corporations is inferred as unwelcome.

cut-welfare.rationale: Later national liberals opposed welfare spending, yet the party also worked with Bismarck's government; adherents were split and the programme says nothing on welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership contradicts the individual-property liberalism and big-business orientation of the party.

surveillance-ok.rationale: It backed the Anti-Socialist Laws, reluctantly, accepting extraordinary police powers against perceived internal threats; the terrorism framing is anachronistic, so inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Described as moderate social conservatism; drug legalisation was not an issue, so a mildly negative answer is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The programme demands abolition of press taxes and caution money and freedom of the press, though the party also backed Kulturkampf curbs on clergy speech; inferred from press freedom.

strong-leader.rationale: The programme demands ministerial responsibility, budget rights and legality of administration, which cut against a leader bypassing parliament, although the party accepted Bismarck's dominance in practice.

state-harmful.rationale: The party sought a unified state endowed with both power and freedom and built the Reich's institutions, so it regarded the state as indispensable.

limit-guns.rationale: An order-minded legalist party would likely accept regulated weapons; there is no documented position, so this is a low-confidence inference.

empower-police-military.rationale: The founding party generously approved armaments and later backed fleet and military expansion, while also asking for burden relief in peacetime.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Moderate social conservatism and Protestant middle-class morality suggest opposition; the issue is not addressed in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: The programme insists on the unitary central power and extending central jurisdiction to all matters concerning the whole, though it also favours communal self-administration.

rehabilitation.rationale: The programme calls for independent courts and jury trial but says nothing about prison purpose; adherents' views are unrecorded.

traditional-family.rationale: Sources describe national liberalism as moderate social conservatism, and its successor party stressed Christian family values.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; moderate social conservatism implies opposition, inferred from the ideology's general character.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology's moderate social conservatism and Protestant middle-class base suggest opposition.

more-religion-public.rationale: The party backed the Kulturkampf and secular schooling against church influence, so a larger public role for religion runs against its record.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; the ideology stresses equality before law, not active corrective programmes, so a mildly negative answer is inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; moderate social conservatism implies adherents would not endorse it, inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nationalism is the defining half of the ideology, including defence of national language and culture in contested regions.

gradual-change.rationale: The programme rejects satisfying all demands at once, speaks of the continuing evolution of the constitution and of working within existing institutions step by step.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not addressed in the sources; the ideology offers no clear line.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Its nationalism put sovereignty in the nation-state; international bodies were not an issue, so inferred.

free-trade.rationale: The party supported free trade in the 1870s and its left wing seceded over the 1879 tariff, though its right wing turned protectionist.

nation-first.rationale: National interest and power are central, as in the programme's demand for a state of both power and freedom.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anachronistic; its foreign policy was national-interest driven, so a human-rights pretext was not its logic. Inferred.

open-borders.rationale: A party built on the nation-state and unitary central power would not envisage open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The party welcomed Germany's transformation into a modern industrial state; limiting growth is inferred as foreign to it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; an industrialist party would resist drastic restrictions, inferred from its pro-industry stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: It embraced industrialisation and progress as national strength; the sweeping claim is inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; pro-industry and pro-power outlook suggests support, low confidence.

revolution-justified.rationale: The programme works for liberty through constitutional means and reform in cooperation with the government, rejecting upheaval.

experts-over-public.rationale: Its base was the educated middle class and its leaders were jurists and officials, yet it embraced universal suffrage, so only mildly positive.

central-planning.rationale: Its core was economic liberalism and business interests, in direct opposition to planned economies.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public or worker ownership of businesses is contrary to its propertied, pro-business character.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; landowners and business interests would resist a single land tax, inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Propertied constituency suggests opposition; no documented position.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; unconditional state payments conflict with liberal self-reliance and opposition to welfare spending.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The party was split by the 1879 tariff turn: free-traders seceded in 1880 while a protectionist wing stayed with the conservatives.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Early advocates accepted cooperation with state industry and subsidies for strategic sectors, but later liberals disliked state direction; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: It became the party of big industry and banks, though the programme attacks feudal limits on land and credit; the egalitarian ownership aim is not its goal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing wage labour is a socialist aim in full opposition to this liberal-capitalist party.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The party supported the Reichsbank and a common currency as part of national unification.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The programme seeks to remove estates principles and trade regulation chains, which is opposed to state-recognised bodies fixing wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: It was a parliamentary party committed to constitutional politics and competed with others in the Reichstag.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The programme aims to harmonise a monarchical federal state with constitutional law; national liberals accepted and often favoured constitutional monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The programme welcomes universal suffrage as a bulwark of freedom in time, but German and Austrian national liberals often favoured conservative government, so not strong.

direct-votes.rationale: It put the nation's voice in a representative Reichstag and sought to concentrate parliamentary functions there.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power contradict its parliamentary constitutionalism and propertied outlook.

right-to-secede.rationale: The programme demands a unitary central power and the accession of the southern states; secession threatens national unity.

natural-rulers.rationale: It sought to clear away remnants of the estates system and make equality before law real, against inborn rank, though elites led the party.

political-violence-never.rationale: National liberals backed Prussia's wars for unification and armaments, so absolute pacifism is not their view, but they stressed lawful constitutional methods.

war-builds-character.rationale: Later wings embraced militarism and war aims; the founding liberalism did not hold this doctrine. Split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The party backed the Kulturkampf, subordinating the church to the state, which is neither separation nor church autonomy; adherents split on the best form.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The party rested on rule of law and the secular Kulturkampf state against clerical power.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The programme stresses an independent state judiciary and the state's armaments and national power.

military-superiority.rationale: It backed armaments, the Tirpitz fleet laws and later offensive military policy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nation and state were to coincide, with multi-ethnic states a complication; the party's German nationalism is the basis for a mild yes.

class-struggle-history.rationale: National liberalism sees a national community of interests and fought socialism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The programme aims at equality before the law and equal rights, not outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; its state-centred nationalism does not support group land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: It supported colonial policy and a fleet, making reparations unlikely; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Its unions were national or kin-based (Scandinavism, small-German unification), not by religion or civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Liberal economic doctrine and big-business ties incline toward a positive view of self-interest; not stated outright.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The programme puts liberty, rule of law and press and association rights as demands, though duty to the nation was strong.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Anachronistic; industrial modernising outlook suggests instrumental view.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; a growth-minded national party would not favour limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The party welcomed industrial transformation and represented big industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: It favoured industrial progress but within gradual reform and respect for institutions, so disruption is not welcome.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; moderate social conservatism suggests wariness.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; its accountability demands (ministerial responsibility) do not fit rule by algorithm.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; the party tolerated extraordinary state powers of surveillance against internal enemies.

restore-past-order.rationale: The programme demands abolition of estates principles and manorial police, a progress agenda against old order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Its pragmatic cooperation with Bismarck's government for unification, despite imperfect constitutional gains, reflects a results-first attitude.

direct-action.rationale: It pursued change through elections, the Reichstag and negotiation with government.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A modernising industrial party; the idea is wholly alien.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Industrial liberal capitalism rests on division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist principle opposed to its propertied liberalism.

production-for-use.rationale: Opposed to profit-based market economy it championed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist claim rejected by a party of industry and banks.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: It backed the Anti-Socialist Laws and rejected socialist revolution.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation conflicts with its private-property liberalism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: It supported capitalism and regarded war as a matter of state policy, not an economic inevitability.

taxation-theft.rationale: It built a strong state and its finances (Reichsbank, taxes, budget rights); taxation is legitimate when parliament approves.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal in civil liberties, yet it backed Kulturkampf and Anti-Socialist restrictions beyond harm prevention; adherents split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The programme emphasises individual equality before law, but nationalism treats the nation as a rights-bearing community.

conscription.rationale: The programme accepts the army and military service, asking only to shorten it; the Reich was built on universal conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: It demanded a voice in parliament as the bulwark of freedom, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Not stated; the party saw the state as embodying national power and law, not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Its liberty was legal and constitutional (press, assembly, rule of law), not material provision.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; educated classes were its base and it did not see them as hostile.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents' views unrecorded.

organic-representation.rationale: The programme aims to remove estates principles and to rest on universal suffrage and a parliament.

total-state.rationale: Its goal was a state of power and freedom with legal limits, independent judiciary and civil liberties.

national-rebirth.rationale: It sought unification and gradual constitutional development, not radical rebirth rhetoric, though later wings used nationalist exaltation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: It supported colonial, naval and, in WWI, extensive annexationist aims.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The programme demands abolishing manorial authority and estate privileges for modern law.

bound-labor.rationale: It attacks limits on freedom of movement and manorial power; bound labour is the opposite.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Rationalist liberal outlook inclined toward objective knowledge; not addressed in the sources.

universal-morality.rationale: Liberal rationalism implies universals; not a documented position.

single-common-good.rationale: The programme balances interests and works by compromise with government; liberal pluralism of interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anachronistic; liberals like Lasker, a Jewish National Liberal, pursued emancipation in Germany, and the question was unaddressed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nationalist logic supports co-nationals' return, though the issue is not stated.

revive-national-language.rationale: National liberalism in Finland, Hungary and elsewhere promoted national language, though not a German issue.

school-vouchers.rationale: It favoured state control of schools, but also freeing primary schools from crippling regulations; vouchers anachronistic.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Its programme sought budget approval rights and economy, and its liberalism favoured sound finance; Keynesian stimulus anachronistic.

economic-freedom.rationale: The party paired economic liberalism with political freedom, though it accepted limited political freedom with strong state at times.

rule-by-example.rationale: It demanded legal responsibility of ministers and officials, rather than reliance on rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.rationale: National unity is its highest task and the doctrine is the heart of national liberalism.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; its power-state and military outlook implies willingness to act without outside approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rationalist yet Protestant and morally conservative; not stated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nationalist logic favours reserving benefits for citizens; not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Self-help liberalism and moderate social conservatism incline to work requirements; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: It sought national unity over class struggle and later opened toward parties further left.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Gradual evolution and respect for institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Anachronistic; the Reich was itself a power among Western great powers.

workers-nation.rationale: It aimed to integrate workers in the national state rather than international socialism, and fought the Social Democrats.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Moderate social conservatism and nineteenth-century norms imply support; not addressed.

ban-interest.rationale: It represented banks and commerce, and its liberalism accepted credit; the programme criticises the freezing of credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: It stood for equality before the law and ending estate privileges.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist thesis opposed by a party that saw the state as the national community.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; industrial modernisers would favour domestic energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist assimilation of minorities is typical; not directly addressed.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory outside national-liberal tradition.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Reichstag used district majority voting that the party worked within; PR not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Weltpolitik wings felt a German mission, but the founding party stressed unity and freedom at home.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not a concept in its tradition; moderate social conservatism rejects it.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: It was itself a governing, elite party of notables and tied to Bismarck.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics not addressed in sources; liberal individual rights counsel against.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The programme demands that all officials answer for their actions legally, though past killings are not mentioned.

night-watchman-state.rationale: It built Reich institutions and law and supported national-economic infrastructure beyond minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed; liberal equality counsels against.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Programme aims at guaranteed equality before the law and removal of estate privileges.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-internal question; the party was simply opposed to socialism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: It supported colonial settlement and rarely called states colonial projects.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: It sought uniform law (Lasker's codification) and equal rights across the state, and supported civil marriage in the Kulturkampf.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Rights of association and conscience point against it, though it did not address conversion directly.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an issue in its tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Its successor party stressed secular education and the party supported Kulturkampf school control.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine; national liberals rejected socialist states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The programme rests on a nation of equal citizens voting by universal suffrage and a parliament controlling the budget.

trade-surplus.rationale: Free-trade wing disliked mercantilism, but protectionist wing sought export strength.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to rule of law and equality principles; later nationalist wings may differ.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: It backed Prussian wars and military power, so it rejects the absolute rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Economic liberalism and later nationalist wings both embraced competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: It backed the Anti-Socialist Laws that banned socialist organisations.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: It condemned arbitrary government before 1866 and demanded legal responsibility of officials, though not in republican terms.

separated-powers.rationale: The programme demands an independent judiciary, budget rights and ministerial responsibility.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist doctrine opposed to its liberalism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: It was a party of propertied classes; no priority for the poor in its programme.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial wing opposed socialist labour organisation; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; liberal political economy includes both Malthusian and institutional views.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nation-state nationalism assumed shared language and culture as the basis of unity, and multi-ethnic states were seen as a problem; not directly stated.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The programme depends on elections and independent professional officials.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: It accepted the Anti-Socialist Laws, reluctantly, as exceptional measures.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing contradicts market liberalism; wartime exceptions are likely.

party-controls-media.rationale: It demanded press freedom and abolition of newspaper taxes.

party-commands-army.rationale: It aimed at a constitutional state and parliamentary budget control over armed forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Nationalist caution on citizenship; not documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: It wanted daily allowances so ordinary persons could stand, not pay capped at workers' wages.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: A party of notables with notorious factions and splits, and not binding discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Its aim was a unitary nation-state, not a supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: It accepted the monarchical constitution, where the Kaiser commanded forces and chose ministers, while seeking ministerial responsibility.

church-by-bishops.rationale: A Protestant base which supported state supervision of churches; no episcopal doctrine.

clerical-rule.rationale: It fought political Catholicism in the Kulturkampf.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: It backed the government's war aims in WWI.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Press freedom is a programme item, though moral conservatives among them might censor; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Constitutional limits and accountability favoured; not stated.

recall-officials.rationale: The programme prefers legal responsibility of officials and representative institutions to recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: It backed a strong military and great-power politics.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Property-respecting but market-friendly; the idea is socialist/radical.

people-in-arms.rationale: It accepted standing army and universal service but not militia in place of professionals.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: It was an urban, industrial and commercial party, and opposed agrarian subsidies.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The programme demands accession of southern Germany, a nation split by the 1866 settlement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The educated Protestant middle class was its core base.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nineteenth-century nationalism and imperial attitudes ranked cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Imperial Germany retained capital punishment; moderate conservatism inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; moderate social conservatism implies opposition.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Its modernising rationalist outlook rejects it; unstated.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: German nationhood and later nationality law followed descent; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: National liberals backed assimilating policy (Hungary, Prussian Poland), inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Equality before a uniform law favours no exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Moderate social conservatism and national conformity; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anachronistic; the party sought political unity without transforming property.

constituent-assembly.rationale: It preferred evolving the existing constitution with the government, though the North German constitution came from a constituent Reichstag.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: It argued unity and liberty go together, so freedom is not traded for growth, though it accepted Bismarck's methods.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; great-power outlook suggests independence in arms.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Its head of state was a hereditary monarch; no presidential question.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Supported the Reichsbank and sound gold currency; anachronistic framing.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: It treated property as a core liberal right, with limits set by law.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate internal to the left; no documented stance.

collective-defense.rationale: Its great-power and alliance-friendly nationalism favours it; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: It backed the 1866 Prussian annexations; this view is opposed to its record.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: It strongly backed the Kulturkampf, subordinating churches to civil authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A constitutional monarch as national symbol suited the monarchical federal state it accepted.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Its unitary central power conviction implies willingness to preserve unity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The programme seeks uniform law and unitary power, but protects the advanced institutions of newly annexed provinces.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Constitutionalism and legal responsibility exclude sacral rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No documented position; propertied liberalism did not have a doctrine on this.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; liberals stressed education and environment while nationalists stressed innate national character, so adherents are split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Its core was rule of law and legal responsibility of ministers.

mixed-constitution.rationale: It aimed to reconcile monarchy, federal states and a popularly elected parliament.

leader-cult.rationale: Constitutionalism and legal accountability oppose the cult of a leader.

land-redistribution.rationale: It defended property and credit and the propertied classes.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Hungarian and Pan-German-linked wings claimed co-ethnics' interests, but the founding programme aimed only at unifying Germany.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Opposed to religious coercion and liberal rights.

women-must-cover.rationale: Liberal freedom in dress; not an issue historically.

common-currency.rationale: It supported the Goldmark and common national currency, though not across states.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Scandinavism and German unification are examples of kin unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: It favoured assimilative national state and Germanisation of minorities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: German Jewish liberals like Lasker fought for rights within Germany; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis opposed by nationalism that credits ideas and political will.

ban-cartels.rationale: The party was close to big business and cartels; cartel breaking is unlikely.

no-bailouts.rationale: Liberal market logic opposes bailouts; no specific stance.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The programme demands independent judiciary and rule-of-law limits on government.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Its liberal wing championed trade and the party was industrial and export-minded; autarky was alien.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; business party would resist binding standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: A market-liberal party relies on material incentives.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The programme seeks to abolish manorial authority and estate privileges, though it retained monarchy and reformed rather than abolished the House of Lords.

history-own-civilization.rationale: National culture and identity formation are central to national liberalism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: It supported colonial policy; imperial justifications inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: National identity and loyalty to the national state are central to the ideology and the party's national-school outlook, though liberals also wanted primary schools freed from crippling regulation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Equality before law implies no racial preferences; anachronistic.

public-money-creation.rationale: It supported a banking system and Reichsbank with gold currency.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A party of industry saw capitalism as adaptable and rejected collapse theories.

delink-world-market.rationale: It championed trade and industry integrated in the world market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis opposed by national liberalism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Economic liberty argues yes, equality before the law argues no; anachronistic.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The programme demands press, assembly and association guarantees and constitutional strengthening.

elective-rulers.rationale: It accepted the hereditary monarchy within a constitutional federal state.

minority-veto.rationale: Parliamentary majority rule and national unity oppose individual veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Its response to the constitutional conflict was lawful pressure and later cooperation after indemnity, not removal.

parliament-supreme.rationale: It wanted strong budget rights and ministerial responsibility but accepted a monarchical constitution; split on supremacy.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; the conventional view is inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Moderate social conservatism implies duties of the privileged; unstated.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The party insisted that the people and representatives must be active in public affairs.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian view; not its own.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory; its business outlook rejects it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equality before law implies no native-birth reservation, though not addressed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed; unification, not revanchism, was its aim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; the question did not exist for the historical party.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Hostile to both radical right and left; anachronistic.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources; no basis for a position either way.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources; no basis for a position either way.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: National liberals favoured constitutionalism but often adapted it to national conditions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: It wanted army under constitutional control, though the Prussian army was loyal to the crown.

paid-care-work.rationale: Anachronistic; moderate social conservatism and liberal economics.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The programme calls the full right of approving the budget the first reform needed, after the budget-less years of the Prussian constitutional conflict.

filial-duty.rationale: Not a party issue; inferred from the conservative bourgeois family morality of the German middle class it represented.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from its support for a professional, rule-bound Rechtsstaat bureaucracy and educated-elite leadership, rather than patronage.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred as split: its free-market wing opposed controls, while its nationalist and big-business wing favoured protecting national industry.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from its anticlerical Kulturkampf stance, which backed civil marriage and state over church authority, though not from any stated divorce position.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from its model of independent parliamentary representatives within a constitutional monarchy; binding mandates were a radical-democratic idea it rejected.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred as split: its liberal self-help outlook disfavours state insurance, but pensions as private accounts were not an issue of its era.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from its property-owning middle-class base and liberal defence of private property and free disposal of land.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from its nation-building aim of a unified German state, and its later hostility to Polish-language rights in the eastern provinces.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed in its programme; inferred as split between liberal property rights and nationalist protectionism.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its liberal formal legal equality and rule of law, which judges acts and not group outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from its pro-industry, pro-growth liberalism, though educated-bourgeois moralism may have disliked luxury.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split between support for kindred nationalist movements and a preference for stable diplomacy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split, since its strong-state nationalism favoured German power but it stressed constitutional order.

corporate-influence.rationale: The party was close to big business and saw business influence as normal; inferred from its middle-class and industrial base.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: National liberals prized a strong national state, so limits on foreign money are inferred as acceptable; NGOs as such did not exist.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; national strength favoured population growth but the party limited-state liberalism cut against payments.

residents-only-property.rationale: Economic liberals defended free property markets and national unity, so local residency limits are inferred as unwelcome.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic liberalism and self-help left no place for the state as employer of last resort; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism was mixed with power politics and later imperial expansion, so adherents were split; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rule of law and constitutional order were central to the party, so obedience to law as such is inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: The party backed strong national power and later colonial expansion, so a ban on all intervention is inferred as unwelcome.

industrial-unions.rationale: A party of big industry and propertied citizens was reluctant about labour organisation; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Kulturkampf cast political Catholicism as hostile to the nation, so suspicion of a minority is inferred, though the liberal party did not hold conspiracy doctrines.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The party built the civil, legal order and codification; abolishing legal marriage is inferred as contrary to that.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The founding program asked for constitutional government and publicity of the state affairs; a right to records is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Economic liberals favoured trade and efficient production; the party leaned toward free trade before the 1879 tariffs.

informal-organisation.rationale: National liberals were a party of parliamentary organisation and formal institutions; informal groups are inferred as unsuited.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The party put the national constitution and unified state first; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Nation was defined by state and culture, and the party fought clerical influence; religion as the defining bond is inferred as unwelcome.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: National liberals sought a sovereign nation-state among equals; ritual submission to a leading power is inferred as unwelcome.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The party built a unified Reich with national finances and constitutional centralism; inferred that retention by regions would be opposed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The 1867 programme and its liberal outlook defend property and a free economy; common ownership of production is inferred as rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: The party backed the anti-socialist laws and opposed socialist movements; inferred stance toward communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: A free-economy liberalism with a limited state is inferred to accept private and independent providers within public systems.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Kulturkampf was aimed at clerical influence, but liberal Protestants did not view religion as an illusion fading with material change; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The party represented industry and business and favoured a free economy; inferred that capitalism was seen as progress.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Bourgeois liberalism of the period did not see women's equality as requiring economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Self-help liberalism favoured families and private arrangements over public domestic services; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: German nationalism of the period included language purism, but liberals were not united on it; inferred, adherents split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Rule-of-law liberalism favours binding treaties, but nation-building priorities could override them; inferred, split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: A liberal, national-state and market programme is opposed to communal property societies; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: National liberals backed the Germanising settlement policy in Prussian Poland; inferred from their nationalism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: National liberals took capitalism, in liberal form, as the sound basis while rejecting socialism; inferred.

missingStatements.text: A strong nation-state is the necessary condition for the freedom of its citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: The founding programme's motto is that the German state and German freedom must be achieved simultaneously and through the same means.

missingStatements.text: A government must have its budget approved by an elected parliament before it may spend.
missingStatements.rationale: The programme calls the full right of approving the budget the first reform needed, after the budget-less years of the Prussian constitutional conflict.

missingStatements.text: Ministers and officials should be legally answerable for their official acts.
missingStatements.rationale: The programme demands laws establishing the effective responsibility of ministers and all state officers on the principle that everyone must answer for their actions.
missingStatements.declined: Ministerial responsibility is accepted by nearly every constitutional ideology, so it would not separate ideologies; the bank is kept lean and budget-needs-parliament covers the parliamentary-control claim.

notes: The party was never uniform: a liberal Rechtsstaat wing (Lasker, the 1880 Secession) and a Nationalstaat or power wing (Miquel, later Bassermann) answered differently on tariffs, welfare, imperialism and parliamentary government. The profile follows the mainstream before the 1890s, with later strands noted in rationales. Many modern-issue answers are low-confidence inferences.
